text.p: Australian government officials, looking for safeguards against conflicts of interest, said on Monday that blind trusts might be a worthwhile measure but not a total solution.

"The report .... concludes that blind trusts and management agreements do not provide a complete solution to problems of conflict of interests for officeholders," Prime Minister John Howard said, commenting on a report from the bureaucracy.

"They could, however, be worthy of greater examination to see if they are appropriate additions to the range of available measures," he said in a statement, adding that the government would consider the report further.
Two government members quit last year over conflicts of interest.
